summary: Milestone 2026.05.244 is a planning-only milestone with 0 experiments completed — the twentieth consecutive empty-timing-window retrospective. The 13-task roadmap (exp2530–exp2542) was validated and pre-staged, with IsingVerifier implementation (exp2531), ensemble v7b regression fix (exp2533), and LaTeX compile repair (exp2536) as top priorities. Both RTX 3090 GPUs remain idle at 0% utilization with 5 MB allocated each, indicating the persistent planning-execution gap has not yet been closed.
bottlenecks_identified: Planning-execution gap: experiments are planned but not activated within the same conductor session, producing an empty timing window every milestone.
No compute-bound experiments ran this milestone, so GPU utilization cannot be assessed; both RTX 3090s are idle at 0% with 5 MB allocated each.
Retro task fires before any experiments complete, yielding 0-experiment retrospectives that consume turn budget without actionable data.
improvements_suggested: Activate exp2530 (archive .244 + activate .244) in the same conductor session as planning, not a separate turn.
Deploy persistent conductor daemon to eliminate the session-boundary gap between planning and execution.
Gate the retro task (exp2542) on minimum experiment count >= 1 so that a zero-experiment retrospective cannot be written until at least one task has landed.
Wire the conductor pre-activation guard to halt and emit a diagnostic when the timing window contains zero experiment commits at retro time.
top_3_highest_leverage_actions: Same-session activation: immediately activate exp2530 after planning completes — this alone closes the planning-execution gap that has caused 20 consecutive empty retros.
Persistent conductor daemon: deploy a long-running conductor process that survives between turns so experiment activation does not depend on a new session being opened.
Retro gate on experiment count: add a conductor check that blocks exp2542 (retro) from activating until experiments_completed >= 1, converting empty retros into forward-only diagnostic blocks.
meta_reflection: The twentieth consecutive empty-timing-window retrospective confirms a structural gap: the conductor's planning and execution phases run in separate sessions with no bridging mechanism, so every milestone's timing window captures zero experiment commits. The improvements suggested here are identical to those from the preceding nineteen retros — suggesting the retro output itself is not feeding back into the conductor's operational config. The highest-leverage change is not another retro suggestion but a mechanical guard (retro gate on experiment count) that makes the empty-retro failure mode impossible rather than merely noted.
